description:
## Goal

Rebalance Elixir-process ownership so the tree-of-record (full session DAG, by_id index, id minting, eventual deferred-flush) lives in `OctoPi.Coder.SessionStore`, and `OctoPi.Coder.Loop` carries only the linearized current path (root-or-latest-compaction → leaf). Compactor and branch-switch share one store read primitive instead of bespoke walks against an in-process struct.

## Why

Today `Coder.Loop`'s `State` carries the entire `SessionManager` struct — `by_id` map, every entry on every branch ever explored, leaf pointer, label index — plus the orchestration responsibilities (extension dispatch, agent FSM bridging, compaction kickoff). The store is a write-only file handle. This conflates two concerns: *what is the conversation right now* (Loop's job) and *what is the historical tree* (Store's job).

Rebalanced, the runtime becomes much simpler: Loop appends to its `:path` list, hands `:path` directly to the compactor, and only re-fetches from the store when *switching* paths (resume, fork, navigate, post-compaction reset).

A side benefit: deferred-flush (upstream's "buffer until first assistant" rule) becomes trivial once writer + buffer state colocate. Tracked separately as a follow-on idea.

## Scope (in)

- Move `SessionManager` struct + tree ops into `SessionStore` GenServer.
- Loop drops `:session_manager`, gains `:path` + thin metadata.
- One canonical store read primitive: `path/2` with `:to` (`:root` | `:latest_compaction` | id).
- Unify post-compaction and post-navigate-tree path-reset on the same primitive.
- Apply `to_llm/1` consistently at all wire edges.

## Scope (out)

- Deferred-flush (separate idea ticket).
- Any change to JSONL format, entry types, compaction algorithm, extension event surface, or upstream parity. **This is purely an Elixir-process-topology refactor.**
- Renaming `SessionStore` / `SessionManager` (mostly — internal modules may consolidate but the public-facing names stay).

## Constraint

This is a port. The on-disk JSONL format and entry semantics are byte-identical to upstream pi-mono before and after this epic. Verify by replaying upstream-generated session files and confirming round-trip byte-stability.

## Done when

- `Coder.Loop.State` no longer references `SessionManager.t()`.
- `SessionStore` is the only process holding `by_id` / `file_entries` / `leaf_id`.
- `Store.path/2` is the single read primitive used by Loop, compactor, and navigate-tree.
- Compactor consumes `state.path` directly (no tree walk per call).
- All existing tests green; upstream JSONL round-trip parity preserved.
title: Rebalance session ownership: store owns tree, loop owns path
